title: Security, governance and compliance concepts on AWS
learningObjective: Describe AWS compliance and governance concepts, encryption options, where security logs live, where to find compliance information, and the services that monitor, audit and protect resources.
foundation: AWS follows many compliance programs (such as ISO 27001, SOC, PCI DSS, HIPAA eligibility). You download AWS's audit reports from AWS Artifact.
Encryption protects data at rest (stored) and in transit (moving).
Logs show what happened: AWS CloudTrail records API activity, Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics and logs, AWS Config records resource configuration.
engineer: Compliance: AWS Compliance programs by industry and geography (for example GDPR, HIPAA, FedRAMP, C5); compliance is shared, and not every service is in scope for every program (check AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program). AWS Artifact gives on-demand reports (SOC, PCI) and agreements (BAA). AWS Audit Manager helps collect evidence.

Encryption: at rest with AWS KMS keys (AWS managed or customer managed) or CloudHSM; in transit with TLS (AWS Certificate Manager for certificates). Many services support server-side encryption, and S3 encrypts new objects by default (SSE-S3).
Logs: CloudTrail (management and data events; trail to S3; CloudTrail Lake), CloudWatch Logs and metrics, VPC Flow Logs, AWS Config history, S3 server access logs, ELB access logs.

Protect and detect: Amazon Inspector (vulnerabilities), Amazon GuardDuty (threat detection), AWS Security Hub (aggregated findings and standards), AWS Shield (DDoS), AWS WAF, Amazon Macie (sensitive data in S3), Amazon Detective (investigation).

Governance and compliance services: CloudWatch (monitoring), CloudTrail and AWS Config (auditing), IAM access reports (access advisor, credential reports), AWS Organizations SCPs, AWS Control Tower (governed multi-account landing zone).

animation.caption: Open 'Security services' and match needs to services.

example.title: Preparing for a PCI audit
body: The team downloads AWS's PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance from Artifact, confirms that the services used are in scope, enables CloudTrail in all Regions with log file validation, uses AWS Config conformance packs, encrypts data with KMS, and reviews findings in Security Hub.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
configuration.cli:
aws cloudtrail create-trail --name org-trail --s3-bucket-name <bucket> --is-multi-region-trail
aws guardduty create-detector --enable
aws securityhub enable-security-hub
aws kms create-key --description app-key

walkthrough.subtitle: An auditor visits. Show them encryption, logs, compliance reports and continuous monitoring.
learn: Encryption in transit and at rest
Where security logs live (CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Config)
Services that find and stop threats
Compliance differs by location, industry and service

steps.label: Audit
steps.title: The auditor asks you to prove it
body: "Is customer data encrypted? Who changed the firewall last Tuesday? Is AWS itself certified? How would you notice an attack?"
Each question has an AWS service that answers it.

steps.label: Encryption
steps.title: Encrypt data at rest and in transit
body: At rest: data stored on disks, in S3 or in databases is encrypted, usually with keys managed in AWS Key Management Service (KMS). In transit: data moving over the network is protected with TLS (HTTPS).
Encryption is a key benefit of cloud security: it's built in and often just one setting.

steps.label: Logs
steps.title: Capture logs that answer "who, what, when"
body: AWS CloudTrail records API calls: who did what, from where, and when. Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics and logs and raises alarms. AWS Config records how each resource's configuration changes over time and checks it against rules.
Together they handle auditing, monitoring and compliance checks.

callout.text: CloudTrail = who made the change (audit). Config = what the resource looked like and whether it is compliant. CloudWatch = performance and alarms.

steps.label: Artifact
steps.title: Show AWS's own compliance reports
body: AWS Artifact is a free, self-service portal for downloading AWS's compliance reports and agreements, such as SOC reports, ISO certifications and PCI attestations.
You give these to auditors to prove the AWS part of the shared responsibility model.

steps.label: Detect
steps.title: Find threats and weaknesses automatically
body: Amazon GuardDuty spots threats, such as unusual API calls or compromised instances, by analysing logs. Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities.
AWS Security Hub gathers findings from these services in one place. AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

steps.label: Where & what
steps.title: Case: a bank in Germany
body: The bank has to meet financial regulations and EU data rules. It checks the AWS compliance programs for its industry and country, keeps data in an EU Region, and confirms that every service it uses is in scope for the certification it needs.
Not every service is covered by every compliance program.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Every auditor question has an answer
body: Encryption, logs, reports and detection, all built in.
recap: KMS + TLS: encryption at rest and in transit
CloudTrail = audit API calls; Config = configuration compliance; CloudWatch = monitoring
GuardDuty threats, Inspector vulnerabilities, Security Hub in one view, Shield DDoS
Compliance needs differ by country, industry and service
